links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 6, Lists
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: list basics, methods, sequence types, references and the two programs.

links.title: 3. An Informal Introduction to Python
links.why: The tutorial's first account of lists: indexing, slices as shallow copies, and assignment to a slice.

links.title: 5. Data Structures
links.why: Every list method, list comprehensions, the del statement, tuples and the looping techniques, with runnable examples.

links.title: Built-in Types
links.why: The reference for sequence operations, the mutable sequence table and why in-place methods return None.

links.title: copy — Shallow and deep copy operations
links.why: The exact difference between a shallow and a deep copy, from the module that does both.

links.title: random — Generate pseudo-random numbers
links.why: choice, shuffle and sample: which change the list, which return a new one, and what an empty sequence does.

links.title: Programming FAQ
links.why: Why [[None] * 2] * 3 shares one row, how to copy lists, and why a_tuple[i] += ['item'] both fails and works.

links.title: Sorting Techniques
links.why: Key functions, the reverse argument and the guarantee that sorts are stable.

links.title: PEP 202 – List Comprehensions
links.why: Why the for-and-if form for building a list was added.

links.title: PEP 3132 – Extended Iterable Unpacking
links.why: The catch-all starred name in an assignment, as in first, *rest = items.

links.title: PEP 448 – Additional Unpacking Generalizations
links.why: Several * unpackings inside a list, tuple or set display, as in [*a, *b].

links.title: Python Tutor
links.why: Paste a program and step through it line by line, with lists and the names that point at them drawn as boxes and arrows.

_note: Every url was opened with a page fetch and its content read on the date in 'checked'; titles are those of the pages. The documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.7, while the chapter research read the 3.14.4 sources. The textbook chapter's page title was not returned by the fetch, so its title is the chapter's name and its section headings (32 headings, from 'List Data Type' to 'Practice Questions') were what was read. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read, so the page offers labelled searches instead and the course owner may add checked ones here.
